details: The parallel hardware AI runs on: NVIDIA GPUs (H100/B200 class) dominating training and serving, Google TPUs, and inference-focused challengers (Groq LPUs, Cerebras). Accelerator access and interconnect topology, more than any algorithm, set the ceiling of what an organization can train and serve.

explainer.lead: TPU accelerators are the parallel hardware AI runs on, spanning NVIDIA GPUs (H100/B200 class) in training and serving, Google TPUs, and inference-focused challengers such as Groq LPUs and Cerebras. They matter because accelerator access and interconnect topology, more than any algorithm, set the ceiling of what an organization can train and serve.

tiers.eli5: These are the powerful engine rooms computers need to run AI. How many engines you can plug in and how well they talk to each other decides how big a model you can build.
tiers.practitioner: Teams choose among NVIDIA GPUs for training and serving, Google TPUs, and inference-focused challengers like Groq LPUs and Cerebras. A pitfall is to focus on algorithms while overlooking accelerator access and interconnect topology, which cap what can be trained and served.
tiers.paperLevel: The category covers NVIDIA GPUs (H100/B200 class) dominating training and serving, Google TPUs, and inference-focused challengers (Groq LPUs, Cerebras). Accelerator access and interconnect topology, more than any algorithm, set the ceiling of what an organization can train and serve.

explainer.example: An organization planning a large training run finds its ceiling set by how many accelerators it can access and how its interconnect is arranged, not by its choice of algorithm.
